  PROBLEM: The guidance says "Run the git commands this command names (`git fetch`, `git checkout -B`, `git merge --no-edit`, `git push`) exactly as written too, with no `2>&1`, no pipe into `tail` or `head`, and no `;` or `&&` chain of `git status` or `git log` reads." The actual steps elsewhere in the command use template variables like `<head ref>`, `<base ref>`, `<head_sha>`. A session filling in those template values with real refs and then running them as separate Bash calls still matches the exising `permissions.allow` rules (`Bash(git fetch *)`, `Bash(git checkout *)`, `Bash(git merge *)`), so no new capability is introduced. The guidance reduces the session's effective scope by telling it to avoid chaining that the Auto-mode classifier would re-intercept. The same guidance in the live `.claude/commands/` copy at line 172 has the identical text and the same properties.
  WHY: Does not fail. The guidance restricts what an unattended session does with already-allowlisted git commands. No new execution surface, no new env var, no new gate, no capability expansion.
